title: Spec Area Records (specs/<name>.records.json)
description: GENERATED by `tools/spec_source.py schemas --write` from area.schema.json. The ledger of an area: what the tools recorded (check results, witness and refusal verdicts, freshness pins, verification log, traceability, provenance) and the three triage ledgers. Written through spec_source.save_area(), which refuses to change anything authored.

written_against.description: sha256 from `tools/itf_tools.py spec-sha <area>` — the semantic spec content this brief was written for. Mismatch means the spec moved and the brief may describe something no longer there.

check_results.description: Latest Apalache results. Overwritten by /spec-check each run.

max_steps.description: The CONFIGURED Apalache step ceiling for this run (apalache.max_steps). With the two-pass ladder it is no longer the depth every check reached — that is per check, in checks[].steps — so it serves as the fallback bound for records written before that field existed, and as the number a budget-stopped check is honest about NOT having reached.

extraction.description: Code→spec coverage stats from the last tools/spec-extract-audit.py run. The third completeness axis, and the only one that measures the specification against the implementation rather than the other way round.

simulation.description: Result of the last ADVISORY simulator pre-gate (`quint run`, spec-record check step 0). Deliberately kept apart from `checks`: the simulator's '[ok] No violation found' means 'not in the executions I explored', which is not a verdict, so nothing here ever becomes a formal_status and the readback must never render it as a ✓. What it is for: a shallow bug reported in seconds instead of after the model-checking run, and a witness the random search never reaches flagged before Apalache is asked to find it.

backend.description: Evaluator used. Absent when the installed quint predates `quint run --backend` and its own default was used.

max_samples.description: Executions explored. The denominator every count below is honest against.

seed.description: Present only when the run was seeded. Without it the exploration differs run to run, which is the point on a pre-gate but means a finding here is not reproducible by re-running.

result.description: 'ok' is NOT 'verified' — it is 'no violation in max_samples random executions'. Only `checks` carries verdicts.

falsified.description: Quint names the simulator NAMED as violated. Not a verdict — attribution: these are the invariants the model checker's first pass runs FIRST, because they are guaranteed to produce a counterexample and to produce it cheaply. Recorded so that ordering can be read back and checked; absent when the simulator found nothing or did not say which.

witnesses.description: Per-probe result of `quint run --witnesses`: in how many explored traces the witness predicate held. 0 of N is the vacuity red flag found cheap — a strong hint the behavior is unreachable, and only a hint, because the simulator is incomplete and the model checker still decides.

differential.description: Result of the last differential run: the original implementation and the regenerated one, driven through the same sequences.

sequences.description: How many were actually run. A verdict without this number claims more than it checked.

outcomes.description: External×outcome coverage stats from the last spec-matrix --outcomes run. The failure-behavior twin of `matrix`: same shape, same purpose — make the completeness of the unhappy paths visible in the readback instead of leaving it to memory.

gaps.description: Q-NNN ids of open GAP cells, if any were filed.

matrix.description: State×event coverage stats from the last spec-matrix run (written by spec-matrix --record). Surfaces completeness in readbacks — the gitignored gen/ CSV is the working file, these counts are the reviewable summary.

gaps.description: Q-NNN ids of open GAP cells, if any were filed.

id.description: INV-NNN or PROP-NNN. Witness results live in requirements[].witness, not here.

over.description: Which module produced this result — echoed from the invariant's `over`. A verdict from the probe module was checked against initP/stepP rather than the sidecar's own init/step, and a reader comparing two ✓ marks should be able to see that.

proof.description: Echo of the invariant's proof mode for this check. 'inductive' verified results are unbounded proofs; 'bounded' are valid only to check_results.max_steps; 'structural' results come from the Alloy backend and are valid only within this entry's `scope`.

backend.description: Which validator produced this result. 'alloy' entries are scope-bounded, not step-bounded — their honesty suffix comes from `scope`, not check_results.max_steps. 'tlc' entries come from the temporal path (properties[], `quint verify --temporal`): explicit-state, so they are bounded by the model's own finite state space rather than by check_results.max_steps, and they carry no `trace` because --out-itf is Apalache-only.

alloy_command.description: For backend 'alloy': the .als check command that was run.

scope.description: For backend 'alloy': the finite scope the verdict is valid within, echoed from the run's receipt.json (e.g. '3 Account, 3 User'). A ✓ outside this scope was never checked.

solver.description: For backend 'alloy': the SAT solver id used (pinned via .spec/project.json alloy.solver). Recorded because a scope-bounded ✓ is only reproducible against a named solver.

instance.description: For backend 'alloy': repo-relative path of the counterexample instance XML. Written under specs/<area>/gen/ — GITIGNORED and regenerable, because Alloy picks one instance out of many and its choice is not stable across solver/tool versions. The verdict is committed; the instance is not.

steps.description: Step bound this check actually reached. A verified result is valid only to this depth — may be lower than check_results.max_steps when the run's budget stopped the deep pass. Absent on results that have no step bound at all (inductive proofs, Alloy, z3, TLC temporal) and on records written before the two-pass ladder existed; the readback falls back to check_results.max_steps for those.

batched.description: This verdict came from the batched `quint verify --invariants` run that checked every bounded invariant at once. Same check, same bound, one Apalache start for all of them — recorded because a batched ✓ and a per-id ✓ should not be indistinguishable when reading a ledger back.

note.description: Mechanical note about HOW the result was obtained, never about what it means. Written for results whose usual evidence is absent by construction — e.g. a temporal counterexample found by TLC, which produces no ITF trace.

trace.description: Counterexample ITF path relative to specs/, if any.

counterexample.description: NL explanation of the counterexample (nl_explanation). The raw trace lives in the file at `trace`, not inline.

conformance.description: Trace-replay results from this run (see conformance section).

traceability.description: Maps each requirement/invariant to its Quint construct, the component implementing it, and the code/test locations. Filled in by /spec-code-generate.

generated_from.description: The spec version this area's CODE was generated against, stamped mechanically by `spec-record stamp <area> --generated` at the end of /spec-code-generate. verification_log records that a spec and a code commit were once checked together; this records what the code was BUILT TO, which is a different fact and the one that decides whether regenerating is safe. Absent on any area generated before this block existed, and on every hand-written one — absent means unknown, never means current.

spec_sha.description: git HEAD of the SPEC repo at generation. Locates the exact spec text; moves on every commit, including ones that changed nothing this code depends on.

spec_content_sha.description: itf_tools compute_spec_sha of the area at generation — a hash of the CLAIMS (EARS fields, modality, invariant statements, constraint values, entity states, scope), not of the file. This is the one worth comparing: it moves when the spec's meaning moves and stays put through bookkeeping churn, so `generated-from-stale` fires on a real divergence rather than on a re-run of the checker.

code_sha.description: git HEAD of the CODE repo immediately after generation — the commit the generated code landed in.

code_repo.description: Logical repo name from project.json repos, for the multi-repo case.

extracted_from.description: The code version this area's spec was READ OUT OF, stamped mechanically by `spec-record stamp <area> --extracted` after a brownfield extraction or a re-extraction. Its whole purpose is to give re-extraction a commit range: with it, `spec-record changed <area>` shows WHAT changed since the spec was read; without it, re-extraction can only report which fingerprints are new, never what moved or when. Fingerprints stay the identity mechanism — they survive reformatting and rebases, which a sha does not. This adds the narrative, it does not replace them.

code_sha.description: git HEAD of the code repo when the spec was read from it.

code_path.description: Subtree the extraction read, relative to the code repo root. Narrows the diff to what the spec actually claims to describe.

extraction_triage.description: COMMITTED triage of code sites against the spec — the only check in the framework that runs code → spec rather than spec → code. Every branch, guard literal and error handler in a traced file either maps to a spec element or is explained here. This is where the branches that make a regenerated implementation differ actually live: they are never in the spec, so nothing spec-shaped can look for them.

file.description: Path relative to the code root.

fingerprint.description: Stable hash of the normalized site text, from tools/spec-extract-audit.py. Identity survives the site moving, which a line number does not — a ledger keyed on line numbers rots on the first reformat.

line.description: Advisory only: where the site was last seen.

snippet.description: The site's source text, trimmed. Present so the ledger is reviewable without opening the file.

verdict.description: MAPPED: realizes the spec element in maps_to. NOT-BEHAVIOR: logging, metrics, tracing — real code, no externally observable behavior. DEFENSIVE: unreachable by construction, kept as a belt. DEAD: unreachable, and that is a finding about the CODE. GAP: real behavior nobody has specified — the extraction hole, tracked by a question. OUT-OF-SCOPE: outside the declared boundary; cite the exclusion.

maps_to.description: Required for MAPPED: the spec ids this site realizes (REQ/INV/CON/...).

reason.description: Required for every verdict except MAPPED.

scope_ref.description: Required for OUT-OF-SCOPE: the scope.excluded[].item covering it.

question.description: For GAP verdicts: the open_questions[] entry tracking it.

matrix_triage.description: COMMITTED triage decisions for uncovered state×event cells. The matrix CSV under specs/<area>/gen/ is gitignored scratch — decisions recorded only there would vanish on a fresh clone and the --strict CI gate would fail. This section is the durable home; spec-matrix reads it when regenerating and the CSV merely mirrors it.

verdict.description: GAP: a real hole, tracked by a question. IMPOSSIBLE: the cell cannot occur (a guard forbids it). NO-OP: the event CAN occur here and deliberately changes nothing — the third answer a closed specification needs, and the one most often left implicit; name the requirement that decided it in `reason`. OUT-OF-SCOPE: outside the declared boundary, and must cite the scope.excluded[] entry that covers it.

reason.description: Why: the impossibility argument, the covering artifact, or (for GAP) the unanswered question.

scope_ref.description: Required for OUT-OF-SCOPE: the scope.excluded[].item that covers this cell. Without it, 'out of scope' is an assertion; with it, it is a reference to a boundary someone reviewed.

question.description: For GAP verdicts: the open_questions[] entry tracking it.

outcome_triage.description: COMMITTED triage for external×outcome cells no requirement handles — the failure-behavior twin of matrix_triage. Same verdicts, same durability rationale: the generated view under specs/<area>/gen/ is gitignored scratch, this is the reviewable home.

verdict.description: GAP: a real hole, tracked by a question. IMPOSSIBLE: the cell cannot occur (a guard forbids it). NO-OP: the event CAN occur here and deliberately changes nothing — the third answer a closed specification needs, and the one most often left implicit; name the requirement that decided it in `reason`. OUT-OF-SCOPE: outside the declared boundary, and must cite the scope.excluded[] entry that covers it.

reason.description: Why: the impossibility argument, the covering artifact, or (for GAP) the unanswered question.

scope_ref.description: Required for OUT-OF-SCOPE: the scope.excluded[].item that covers this cell.

question.description: For GAP verdicts: the open_questions[] entry tracking it.

additionalProperties.description: Machine-written fields of one record (requirement, invariant, property, constant), keyed by its id.

status.description: Written by `spec-record verify` on a green replay; overrides the authored @status.

'witnessed' = a trace shows the behavior happening. 'no-witness' = UNREACHABLE (impossible guard or missing action). 'hollow' = the predicate was ALREADY TRUE before anything happened: the checker returned a single-state counterexample, so the trace shows the initial state satisfying the predicate, not the behavior occurring. A hollow witness is a false proof and gates exactly like a missing one — the usual fix is a witness.delta forcing the step to move the state, and often a predicate that was too weak to distinguish before from after.

trace.description: ITF trace path relative to specs/, e.g. 'auth/traces/REQ-003.itf.json'. Written by /spec-check.

steps.description: Step bound the probe actually ran to. A 'no-witness' is only as strong as this number — unreachable within 3 steps is a very different claim from unreachable within 10, and when the run budget stops the deep pass the shallow bound is what stands. Absent on records written before the two-pass ladder existed.

model_sha.description: sha256 of the model the trace was found against (.qnt + .probes.qnt; see `tools/itf_tools.py sha <area>`). spec-lint FAILs when this no longer matches — a trace from an older model proves nothing about the current one.

outcomes.description: Per permitted outcome of a `may` requirement, keyed by outcome name.

status.description: Same values as witness.status; 'hollow' means this outcome's predicate already held in the initial state.

trace.description: ITF trace path relative to specs/.

steps.description: Step bound this outcome's probe actually ran to — same honesty rule as witness.steps.

written_against.description: sha256 from `tools/itf_tools.py meaning-sha <area>` — the requirement content this meaning restates. Mismatch means the requirement moved and the plain-words sentence may describe something no longer specified.

witnessDelta.description: The PRE-state the witnessing step must start from. A postcondition alone proves reachability, not causation: a guard that already implies its own postcondition makes the action a no-op that only fires once its result already holds, and the probe goes green over dead text. The probe conjoins this over `_prev*` ghosts snapshotted before the step, so the trace must show the state actually MOVING. Referenced from BOTH the witness (a `must` has one) and each permitted outcome (a `may` proves each outcome with its own probe, so each names its own pre-state) — tools/spec-probes.py reads outcomes[].delta, which this schema previously forbade outright.

pre.description: Quint boolean over the `_prev*` ghost vars, true exactly when the pre-state was one this behavior could still change. For a lockout: `_prevAccountStatus.get(_lastUid) == Unlocked`.
